newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end up amid continued bullishness.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end up amid continued bullishness.

text.p: Israeli shares closed broadly higher in heavy turnover on Monday with traders saying that sentiment continues to be very bullish.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of top 100 shares rose 1.98 percent, or 5.14 points, to 265.01 on a very high all-share turnover of 218 million shekels against 188 million shekels on Sunday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 1.86 percent higher at 271.93.

"The market looks too good. It's rising very fast with no selectivity at all. There are only a few sellers and many investors want to enter the market. The rise has nothing to do with politics or the economy," said Doron Tsur, head of research at Sahar Securities.

"The main reason for today's rise is that the mood is very positive and investors believe that the market will continue to rise," a trader at Bank Leumi said, adding that foreign investors were very active buyers today.

Tsur was less optimistic about the outlook. "I'm sure that after the publication of fourth-quarter (earnings) reports the market will become more selective. There is simply no justification for such a broad rise," he said.

The most active shares were Israel Chemicals, which rose 3.75 percent to 393 agorot on turnover of 9.4 million shekels; Clal Israel, which gained 2.25 percent to 106.5 on volume of 9.3 million shekels; and Bank Leumi, which rose 3.0 percent to 533 on turnover of 8.2 million shekels.
